issue.body:
<!--

## Issue Description

### Expected Behavior

Generating a migration between two tables, one having a enum primary column and a one-to-many / many-to-one relation between them should generate valid SQL, with corrrect enum typing on the table B column statements that reference the primary column of table A


### Actual Behavior

The migration contains column statements that reference a `"NULL"` type enum. It should be `('msGraph', 'atlassian')` etc

```
query: ALTER TABLE `access_event` ADD `employeeProvider` enum NULL
query failed: ALTER TABLE `access_event` ADD `employeeProvider` enum NULL
error: Error: ER_PARSE_ERROR: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near 'NOT NULL' at line 1
```


### Steps to Reproduce

<!--
  Your bug will be investigated much faster if we can run your code and it doesn't
  have dependencies other than TypeORM. Issues without reproduction steps or
  code examples may be closed as not actionable.

  Please try to provide a Minimal, Complete, and Verifiable example.
  http://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve
-->

1. Create a simple entity setup like below
2. Generate a migration
3. Run said migration

```typescript
enum Providers { 
  MS_GRAPH = 'msGraph'
  ATLASSIAN = 'atlassian'
}

@Entity()
export class Employee extends BaseEntity {
  @PrimaryColumn({ type: 'enum', enum: Providers })
  provider!: Providers
  
  @OneToMany(() => AccessEvent, (accessEvent) => accessEvent.employee)
  accessEvents!: AccessEvent[]
}

@Entity()
export class AccessEvent extends BaseEntity {
  @PrimaryColumn({ type: 'varchar', length: 128 })
  id!: string

  @ManyToOne(() => Employee, (employee) => employee.accessEvents)
  employee!: Employee
}
```

Generating a migration from this results in it creating a line like this in the migration: 
```
`ALTER TABLE `access_event` ADD `employeeProvider` enum NULL`
```

It somehow is unable to retrieve the enum values. If I change Employee's primary column to `@PrimaryColumn({ type: 'varchar', length: 128 })` it generates a migration with the correct typing, but not when I use enum. 

### My Environment

I'm running this in my Next.js application 

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    | Ubuntu  20.04  |
| Node.js version     | v14.13.0` | <!-- run `node -v` to obtain this -->
| Typescript version  | v4.0.5 | <!-- run `npm list typescript` to obtain this -->
| TypeORM version     | v0.2.30 | <!-- run `npm list typeorm` to obtain this -->


### Additional Context

The enum is actually stored elsewhere, and verified to be valid. The location has no effect on it


### Relevant Database Driver(s)
